newsitem.title: UK: Don't read anything into Clarke comments-Treasury.
newsitem.headline: Don't read anything into Clarke comments-Treasury.

text.p: The British Treasury said Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's comments in an interview with Sky Television at lunchtime should not be construed as indicating that interest rates had either been changed or left at 6.0 percent.
A Treasury spokesman said some financial market participants appeared to believe he was implying a change had been agreed in interest rates.
"Nothing should be read into the Chancellor's comments at lunchtime either way," the spokesman told Reuters.
In the interview, minutes after the end of the monetary meeting, Clarke said:
"Eddie will announce the decision in due course. That's the arrangement we have."

He later added: "The minutes will come out in due course and I'm sticking to my own rules...in order to avoid unsettlling the markets. Wait to see the minutes and then you'll see the sensible discussion which Eddie George and myself have had."
Minutes of monetary meetings are published six weeks afterwards.
